plan: My value is $20. In the ascending clock auction, I want to stay in as long as the clock price is below my value. Therefore, I want my exit price (sealed bid) to be as high as possible, but not so high that I risk losing out on a profitable opportunity. A reasonable strategy is to bid slightly below my value, say, $19.9. This ensures I stay in the auction until the clock reaches a price very close to my value, maximizing my potential profit if I win.

[My value is $30, which is significantly higher than the usual range of $0-$20. This gives me a considerable advantage. I should bid aggressively to try and secure the win. I want to win if either other bidder has a value below $20. I should bid $20.00. This will ensure I win if both other bidders have a value less than or equal to $20. In the second stage, I will stay in the auction until the price reaches my value of $30. Since my value is so high, I want to ensure I win if either of the other bidders values are less than $20.00. Therefore, I should bid $20.00.]

I should bid slightly below my true value to maximize potential profit while still having a good chance of winning. I will bid $29.9, which is slightly below my value of $30. This ensures that if I win, I will make a small profit, and I avoid overbidding significantly.
